topic: The Great Bridge: Connecting Slopes and Areas (The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus)
target_audience: Senior high school or first-year university students

sections.title: The Runner's Puzzle: A Tale of Two Tasks
lecture_lines: Meet Zippy, our fast cheetah runner.
We can track his position or his speed.
How are distance and speed actually connected?
animations: Animate a circle (color #FFD700, labeled 'Zippy') moving from x=-4 to x=4 across the screen.
Create axes and plot position s(t) = 0.5*t^2 (color #00FF00) on the top half of the screen.
Create a second set of axes and plot velocity v(t) = t (color #FF4500) on the bottom half.

sections.title: Prerequisite Check: Slopes and Sums
lecture_lines: Differentiation finds the slope at any point.
Integration finds the total area under a curve.
Are these two processes related to each other?
animations: Plot f(x) = x^2 (color #00BFFF) and show a tangent line (color #FFFF00) sliding from x=-2 to x=2.
Shade the area under f(x) = x^2 from x=0 to x=2 using color #FF69B4.
Display labels 'Slope: Derivative' and 'Area: Integral' (color #FFFFFF) next to their respective visual components.

sections.title: Accumulation: Building the Area Function
lecture_lines: Imagine area growing as a vertical line moves.
We call this growing space the Area Function, A(x).
As x increases, more area is added.
A(x) tracks the total accumulated area from the start.
Watch how A(x) changes as the scrubber moves.
animations: Plot a smooth curve f(x) (color #00FF00) on the lower half of the screen.
Introduce a vertical 'scrubber' line (color #FFFFFF) at the starting point x=a.
Move the scrubber from x=a to x=b, shading the area under f(x) in light green (#66BB6A) as it moves.
Simultaneously plot the area function A(x) (color #FFEA00) on the upper half of the screen.
Draw a vertical indicator (color #FFFFFF) showing that the height of f(x) matches the slope of A(x).

sections.title: The Fundamental Theorem: The 'Undo' Button
lecture_lines: The rate of area growth is the function's height.
This means the derivative of area is the function.
Integration and differentiation are inverse operations.
One builds the area, the other finds its slope.
This connection is the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus.
animations: Display the equation A'(x) = d/dx [integral from a to x of f(t) dt] (color #FFFFFF) at the top.
Highlight the integral term with a yellow box (#FFFF00) and label it 'Area Function'.
Apply the derivative operator and show the yellow box transforming via ReplacementTransform.
Reveal the final result f(x) in bright green (#00FF00) with a flash effect.
Display the text 'Differentiation and Integration are Inverses' (color #FFFFFF) at the bottom.

sections.title: Application: The Antiderivative Shortcut
lecture_lines: To find area, use the function's antiderivative.
Let capital F be the antiderivative of f.
Area is F at b minus F at a.
For Zippy, speed 2t becomes distance t squared.
Plug in the endpoints to find distance covered.
animations: Display the Evaluation Theorem: integral from a to b of f(x) dx = F(b) - F(a) (color #FFFFFF).
Plot velocity v(t) = 2t (color #FF4500) and shade the region from t=0 to t=3.
Display the antiderivative F(t) = t^2 (color #00BFFF) clearly next to the graph.
Show the step-by-step numerical calculation: F(3) - F(0) = 9 - 0 = 9 (color #FFFFFF).
Move the result '9' into the center of the shaded area and flash it with color #00FF00.

sections.title: Summary: The Beautiful Symmetry
lecture_lines: Calculus links slopes and areas in perfect harmony.
Breaking down and building up are two sides.
This bridge connects the two main pillars of calculus.
animations: Divide the screen vertically; label the left 'Differentiation' and the right 'Integration' (color #FFFFFF).
Draw two circular arrows (color #FFFF00) connecting the two labels to illustrate the inverse relationship.
Display the title 'The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus' (color #FFD700) in the center with a ScaleIn effect.
